entities.summary:
Wepwawetemsaf, Sekhemre Neferkhau's successor pharaoh during the Second Intermediate Period, was a key figure in Ancient Egyptian history. He ruled from circa 1700 BCE to 1675 BCE, marking a pivotal era of instability and foreign influence.

During his reign, Wepwawetemsaf sought to reassert Egypt's dominance over its neighboring kingdoms, including the Hyksos and Nubians. This drive for power led to significant military campaigns and diplomatic tensions with neighboring powers.

The legacy of Wepwawetemsaf can be seen in the eventual reunification of Upper and Lower Egypt under the 17th-dynasty pharaoh Ahmose I, who would go on to found a new capital at Thebes. This reunification marked a turning point in Egyptian history, solidifying the country's position as a major power in the region.

The enigmatic Wepwawetemsaf remains an important figure in the annals of Ancient Egyptian history, his impact felt for centuries to come.
